program.section_heading: Airframe and Powerplant Maintenance Technician — Certificates of Achievement and Associates in Science (Airframe Required Courses)
outcomes: Demonstrate proficient, entry-level aviation maintenance skills in airframe, powerplant, or airframe and powerplant with emphasis on aircraft engines, aircraft structures, and aircraft systems.

Have a working knowledge to inspect, maintain, service and repair aircraft electrical, engine (piston and turbine), airframe structure, flight control, hydraulic, pneumatic, fuel, navigation and instrument systems and other aircraft components specified by Federal Aviation Regulation Part 147.
Obtain the knowledge and skills to pass oral, practical and written Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) examination in general and airframe/powerplant subjects.

notes: The page prints one Program Outcomes list shared by the Airframe, Powerplant and Airframe & Powerplant certificates and A.S. degrees; recorded here for the Airframe A.S.
total_units 41 is the printed 'Required Major Total units' under Airframe Required Courses (Airframe 21 + General Required Courses 20).

The description says the focused Airframe A.S. requires the 41-unit major, General Education, and 'electives as needed to complete a minimum of 60 units'; no degree total is printed in a requirements table, so degree_total is left null and electives_fill_degree is true. Reviewer may wish to treat 60 as the degree total.
The GE pattern is only called 'General Education' (not named, e.g. local GE vs CSU GE); ge_pattern left null.
AERO 118 is printed as 1 unit in the requirements list, but its course description gives 0.5 to 1.5 units (variable, repeatable); the state file stores 0.5.
AERO 055 as printed in the catalog corresponds to closed-list AERO 55.
Powerplant courses (AERO 106, 107, 119) belong to the Powerplant award and are not recorded.
